method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)' (last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed), 37 claims; LICENCE: © The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne; Terms clause 5.2, personal use only; paraphrased and hash-anchored (read at https://www.rch.org.au/ (Terms and Conditions, clause 5.2)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne 'RCH flowcharts for Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)' (management diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1), 8 claims; LICENCE: © The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne; Terms clause 5.2, personal use only; paraphrased and hash-anchored (read at https://www.rch.org.au/ (Terms and Conditions, clause 5.2)). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 rebuilds the hand-written Wave 1 page (which quoted RCH) as a paraphrase. Every Wave 1 claim is carried over and re-anchored in the page as fetched on 2026-09-24. S2 anchors point into a text transcription of the management diagram made in Wave 1; the diagram itself is an image and was not re-read.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Keep the child calm:** upset makes the upper airway obstruction worse.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Call senior help early**, and think about transfer, whenever the airway looks to be getting worse.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Severe or life-threatening croup → nebulised adrenaline plus an experienced senior to support the airway.** Milder croup can usually be treated with a corticosteroid on its own.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **What it is:** a (usually viral) inflammation of the larynx, trachea and upper airway. Parainfluenza is the commonest cause; other respiratory viruses, COVID-19 among them, also cause it, so use infection control. Typical age 6 months to 6 years; symptoms tend to be worse overnight.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Examine selectively,** so that the examination itself does not upset the child more.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Oximetry and blood pressure can be skipped** if taking them would distress the child; they are not needed to manage croup. The throat seldom needs looking at. Keep the carer with the child and let them help with the examination.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Risk factors for severe croup:** earlier severe croup · an already narrowed upper airway · low airway tone from an underlying condition (e.g. trisomy 21, neuromuscular disease) · ⚠️ young age: croup is unusual below 6 months and rare below 3 months, so look for another diagnosis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Findings:** barking cough · stridor · a hoarse cry or voice · sometimes widespread wheeze · increased work of breathing · sometimes fever, but the child does not look toxic.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A loud stridor does not mean a worse obstruction.** When the child is otherwise deteriorating, a quiet stridor can signal that the airway is about to obstruct.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Colour and perfusion:** normal and well perfused in mild and moderate → pale in severe → pale, mottled or blue in life-threatening.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Behaviour:** alert and active (mild) → alert with bouts of mild agitation (moderate) → more agitated, drowsy (severe) → confused, drowsy or agitated, perhaps motionless or drooling (life-threatening).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Stridor:** absent or only on activity or upset (mild) → intermittent at rest (moderate) → continuous at rest or biphasic (severe) → biphasic, or ⚠️ possibly soft (life-threatening).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Breathing rate:** normal (mild) → raised (moderate) → markedly raised or ⚠️ falling (severe) → abnormal, with the child tiring towards respiratory exhaustion (life-threatening).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Accessory muscles:** little or none (mild) → intercostal and subcostal recession with tracheal tug (moderate) → marked recession, tracheal tug and abdominal breathing (severe) → severe sternal recession, poor effort, exhaustion (life-threatening).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Oxygen saturation** stays normal in mild and moderate croup. ⚠️ Hypoxia comes late and can mean complete upper airway obstruction is close.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Stridor on its own**, with no change in behaviour or work of breathing, may not need urgent treatment.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Other causes of upper airway obstruction to consider:** retropharyngeal or peritonsillar abscess (quinsy) · bacterial tracheitis · epiglottitis · burns or trauma to the airway.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **The diagnosis is clinical.** In a typical case do not send swabs or nasopharyngeal aspirates, X-rays or bloods; test only when a differential diagnosis is a real concern.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Do only what will change acute management;** every extra examination or test adds distress and can worsen the symptoms. Keep carers close, the room quiet and the lighting moderate.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Leave the child in the position they choose:** it is the one that keeps their airway most open.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Oxygen is seldom needed.** A child who does need it should be treated as having severe upper airway obstruction, or reconsidered for another diagnosis such as anaphylaxis or asthma.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No steroid for a barking cough alone** when there has never been stridor.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Mild:** think about an oral steroid (dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg, or prednisolone 1 mg/kg) when there is stridor, or a risk factor such as young age or poor access to urgent review.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Moderate:** give an oral steroid (dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg or prednisolone 1 mg/kg); add nebulised adrenaline if symptoms persist or get worse.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Severe:** a senior clinician reviews, in a high-acuity area; give nebulised adrenaline together with dexamethasone 0.6 mg/kg (maximum 12 mg) by mouth, IM or IV.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Life-threatening:** move to resuscitation with senior staff · nebulise 5 mL of adrenaline 1:1000 · 100% oxygen at 15 L/min by non-rebreather mask · an experienced clinician prepares to intubate (croup endotracheal tubes if the unit has them) · dexamethasone 0.6 mg/kg (maximum 12 mg) IM or IV.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Keep repeating nebulised adrenaline** until a senior clinician arrives who can support the airway.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Mild (diagram):** a barking cough alone may need no steroid. If the child has had stridor or has risk factors, consider oral dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg or oral prednisolone 1 mg/kg, and give the dose again the next evening.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', management diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup-diagram.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Moderate (diagram):** oral dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg or oral prednisolone 1 mg/kg, repeated the next evening.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', management diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup-diagram.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Oral steroid not tolerated:** the diagram offers nebulised budesonide 2 mg instead.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', management diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup-diagram.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Moderate, responding well:** home once there is no stridor at rest. If the child worsens, move to the severe pathway.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', management diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup-diagram.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Severe (diagram):** 5 mL of adrenaline 1:1000, nebulised undiluted, plus dexamethasone 0.6 mg/kg (maximum 12 mg) IM, IV or oral.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', management diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup-diagram.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Severe, responding well:** give adrenaline again if severe respiratory distress comes back; discharge can be considered 3 hours after the adrenaline if there is no stridor at rest.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', management diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup-diagram.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Severe, responding poorly or not at all:** repeat the adrenaline, rethink the diagnosis and escalate to senior staff or ICU.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', management diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup-diagram.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Life-threatening (diagram):** senior, ICU and anaesthetic help at once · nebulised adrenaline 1:1000, 5 mL, undiluted · 15 L/min oxygen through a non-rebreather mask · dexamethasone 0.6 mg/kg (maximum 12 mg) IM or IV.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'RCH flowcharts for Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', management diagram on the same page, transcribed in Wave 1, https://www.rch.org.au/uploadedImages/Main/Content/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup-diagram.png, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Home when there is no stridor at rest.** After nebulised adrenaline, watch for 3 hours to make sure symptoms do not return.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Observe for more than 3 hours** if the child came in overnight · lives far from medical care · has had stridor more than once in this illness · has a risk factor for severe croup.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Talk to the local paediatric team** for: severe obstruction · risk factors or diagnostic doubt · age under 6 months · no response to nebulised adrenaline.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Think about transfer** if nebulised adrenaline has not helped, keeps being needed, or the child needs more care than the local hospital is comfortable giving.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Discharge criteria:** at least 3 hours of observation after any nebulised adrenaline. Tell parents to come back if stridor at rest returns even though oral steroids were given.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **No antibiotics** in uncomplicated croup: the cause is viral.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No cough suppressants such as codeine:** they do not change the course or severity, and can depress breathing and add sedation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Cold outdoor air (under 10 °C) might ease moderate croup.** Humidified air has no proven effect on severity, and heliox has not beaten nebulised adrenaline in severe croup.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Currency:** PIC endorsed; page last updated September 2024.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Key evidence cited:** a 2023 Cochrane review of glucocorticoids for childhood croup, and a 2023 randomised trial (Siebert et al., Pediatrics) comparing outdoor cold air with room-temperature air.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis)', last updated September 2024, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Croup_Laryngotracheobronchitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24
